issues.description: IdentityGrammar accepts a sign token on the increment too, which silently allows nonsense like IDENTITY(1, -1) parses but isn't valid T-SQL semantics that match the stated goal.
issues.detail: The PR title says 'neg identity seed' — that's one specific shape. The grammar change adds SignedSegmentGrammar before both numbers. If the intent is only the seed, this is wrong-shape; if both are intentionally allowed, the commit message should say so. State which it is, add a fixture covering the increment-sign case (or refuse it), and move on.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT now allows mixing COLUMN and CONSTRAINT items in the same delimited list, which T-SQL does not permit.
issues.detail: The new shape is DROP <Delimited(COLUMN ... | CONSTRAINT ...)>. Nothing forces homogeneity, so 'DROP COLUMN a, CONSTRAINT b' parses fine. Real T-SQL requires all items be one kind. Either split into two top-level alternatives (one COLUMN-delimited, one CONSTRAINT-delimited) or accept that the parser is permissive and document it. Add a fixture either way.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no test fixture exercising it.
issues.detail: A new accepted token type with zero coverage is exactly the kind of thing that rots. If lcid integers really are valid here, add one line to create_login.sql showing DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033. If not, drop the NumericLiteralSegment branch. Don't ship parser surface area you didn't test.

issues.description: This is THREE-PATCHES submitted as one: table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN, identity sign, ALTER TABLE drop-list.
issues.detail: Four independent grammar changes in one diff. Each is small and reasonable on its own, but bisecting a future regression in CREATE LOGIN to a commit titled 'TSQL parsing issues: ...' wastes the maintainer's time. Future patches like this should be split. Not blocking, but noted.

issues.description: Deletion of the existing alter_table.sql multi-action fixture loses real-world coverage instead of fixing it.
issues.detail: The removed statement ('ADD column_b ... DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS c') was apparently invalid T-SQL per the PR description, fine. But it was working test coverage of mixed ADD+DROP behavior. If T-SQL actually forbids that mix, leave a comment-only example or add a should-not-parse test so the next person doesn't reintroduce it.

issues.description: Top-level OneOf replacing Delimited(OneOf(...)) silently changes the contract: only one action per ALTER TABLE now.
issues.detail: Previously the grammar allowed comma-delimited alter actions at the top level (per the old Delimited wrapper). The new shape allows exactly one. This is probably correct for T-SQL — but it's a behavior change worth one sentence in the commit message so the next person reading 'git blame' knows it was deliberate, not a typo.

review.summary: Four independent grammar fixes bundled into one patch. The patches are individually small and the fixture coverage is decent for the headline cases (table-var index, CREATE LOGIN naked identifiers and nString password, drop-list), but several edges shipped untested: NumericLiteralSegment for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE has no fixture, IDENTITY now accepts a sign on the increment with no test or commit-message acknowledgment, and the new DROP delimited shape permits mixing COLUMN and CONSTRAINT items which T-SQL doesn't allow. The top-level switch from Delimited(OneOf) to bare OneOf is a real behavior change worth one sentence in the commit message. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — tighten the grammar or add the missing fixtures, then land.
